findings.title: The heat-margin text puts all over-rating cases outside the training ranges, but 128 mm also goes over under trained conditions; the confirmed core of review finding R1 was left out, though the review section says the confirmed findings are corrected
findings.what_is_written: L42: "outside the training ranges, every 128 mm seed goes over its rating"; L150-151: "The training ranges were a delay of 0-10 ms, mass x0.9-1.1 and no payload. So the real robot's delay and mass decide how much headroom is left."; L329-330: "0.83-1.01 ... across the cases above, and above it beyond the training ranges"; L359-360: "The medium and low findings it confirmed are the corrections made in this version"
findings.evidence: My script review_d22recheck/added-content/a_inrange.py lists sweep points inside the run records' env_config ranges (delay_steps_range [0,10], mass_scale_range [0.9,1.1], kp [0.9,1.1], force [0.85,1.0], friction down to friction_low_hard 0.3, push_dv_max 1.0, terrain_slope_max_deg 10, terrain_step_max_m 0.04) where summary.heat_worst > 1.0. fore128-s1: mass x1.1 1.006, ramp 8 deg 1.02. fore128-s2: mass x1.1 1.022, ramps 3/5/8 deg 1.035/1.073/1.155. fore128-s3 (11 points): mass x1.1 1.064, ramps 3/5/8 deg 1.096/1.151/1.216, 3 cm step 1.018, friction 1.0 1.003, pushes -0.75..+1.0 about 1.00. fore128-s0: none. Run 3: none. The skeptic's verdict on R1 in review_2026-11-26.json says "What holds ... chiefly that 3 of 4 128 mm seeds go over at mass x1.1 (inside the training range ...)". R1's suggested fix also named the 3-8 deg ramps. The revision includes neither, so the report reads as if 128 mm stays under its rating whenever it runs inside the training ranges.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: inside the training ranges, three of four 128 mm seeds already exceed their rating at mass x1.1 (1.006-1.064) and on the trained 3-8 deg ramps (s1 1.02 at 8 deg, s2 1.04-1.16, s3 1.10-1.22), while run 3 stays under at every in-range point. Change 'the real robot's delay and mass decide' to include terrain. Note in the review section that R1 is only partly addressed.

findings.title: Two 128 mm seeds are said to 'come close', but each is over its rating in a nominal-model case, and the demo walk's 1.006 is left out of the answer
findings.what_is_written: "with the nominal model, two 128 mm seeds come close: seed 2 reaches 1.005 in the gait report with observation noise off, and seed 3 reaches 0.997 at the sweep's nominal point"
findings.evidence: gait_report.json nominal_0.25, fore128-s2: left_fore_pitch 1.0046, which is over 1.0. The demo course is also a nominal model (demo_course.py:72 domain_randomization=False, observation_noise=True, 10 ms). Its walk_0.25 tau_drive_rms over continuous_nm gives 1.0062 for fore128-s3 (left_hind_pitch) and 0.9977 for s2 (my b_demo.py). The report's own table at L141 shows 1.01 for s3.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: 'two 128 mm seeds reach or pass their rating with the nominal model: seed 2 at 1.005 (gait report, noise off), seed 3 at 1.006 on the demo walk and 0.997 at the sweep's nominal point'.

findings.title: The stated friction training range of 0.6-1.0 is not what was trained for most of the run: the low end ramps down to 0.3
findings.what_is_written: "training ranges: delay 0-10 ms, mass x0.9-1.1, friction 0.6-1.0, with steps, ramps, pushes and a 0.3 friction floor"
findings.evidence: trike_env.py (f84a6919) _draw_factors: lo = lo + terrain_scale*(friction_low_hard - lo), friction = uniform(lo, hi). With friction_low_hard 0.3 and the terrain ramp running from 1M to 4M steps (record terrain_ramp_from/to), friction is drawn from [0.3, 1.0] after 4M steps. Each sweep's own settings.training_ranges says "friction": [0.3, 1.0]. The same sentence also leaves out kp x0.9-1.1 and force x0.85-1.0.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'friction 0.6-1.0, widened to 0.3-1.0 as the terrain ramps in (1-4 M steps)', and add kp x0.9-1.1 and force limit x0.85-1.0.

findings.title: The heat message says 128 mm goes over its rating only beyond the training ranges, but three of four 128 mm seeds also go over inside them (trained ramps, +10 % mass), and run 3 never does
findings.what_is_written: L329-330: "With 128 mm the worst drive sits at 0.83-1.01 of its continuous rating at 0.25 m/s across the cases above, and above it beyond the training ranges." L42: "outside the training ranges, every 128 mm seed goes over its rating: ..." L44: "Run 3's 188 mm leg also goes over at those delays (1.20-1.38)."
findings.evidence: Script review_d22recheck/reader/scripts/sweep_in_range.py reads robustness/results/<run>/sweep_<run>.json.gz. It marks a point as inside the training ranges when delay is 0-10 ms, friction 0.3-1.0, mass 0.9-1.1, kp 0.9-1.1, force 0.85-1.0, payload 0 and |push| <= 1.0 m/s. These ranges come from the sweep's settings.training_ranges and from trike_env.py:94-102 and 204-205. Training ramps go up to 10 deg (trike_env.py:196) and steps up to 4 cm (:194). Points inside the ranges with heat_worst >= 1.0: fore128-s0 none; s1 mass x1.1 1.006 and ramp 8 deg 1.020; s2 mass x1.1 1.022 and ramps 3/5/8 deg 1.035/1.073/1.155; s3 11 points, among them mass x1.1 1.064, ramps 3/5/8 deg 1.096/1.151/1.216, the 3 cm step 1.018 and friction 1.0 1.003. Run 3 s0 and s1 have no such point. For 160 mm: s0 31, s1 28, s2 35, s3 1. Appendix F shows the same cells: the 'mass, every body' row 1.1 reads 1.01/1.02/1.06 for 128 s1-s3, and the 'ramp up' rows read 1.04/1.07/1.16 for s2 and 1.10/1.15/1.22 for s3. So 'above it beyond the training ranges' implies that 128 mm stays at or below 1.01 inside the ranges, which is false on trained ramps. The comparison with run 3 also leaves out the place where 128 mm is worse than run 3. The first review's R1 verifier named this point (mass x1.1, inside the range) as the part that holds, at medium severity. The revision does not include it, yet its review section says the confirmed findings 'are the corrections made in this version'. One caveat: 'every body x1.1' is a corner of the per-body training draw. The ramp points alone are clearly inside training.
findings.suggested_fix: L329-330: "With 128 mm the worst drive is at 0.83-1.01 of its continuous rating at 0.25 m/s on flat ground in the four cases above. Inside the training ranges, three of the four 128 mm seeds also go over at some sweep points: on the trained 3-8 deg ramps (s1 1.02 at 8 deg, s2 1.04-1.16, s3 1.10-1.22) and with every body 10 % heavier (s1 1.01, s2 1.02, s3 1.06). Run 3's two seeds stay under at every such point. Beyond the training ranges every 128 mm seed goes over." Add a matching bullet under L42 and an 'Inside the training ranges' bullet before L143. Then amend the review section to say that this part of R1 was missed.

findings.title: The demo course's 'all under the 100 C limit' at 128 mm depends on the 30 s standing breaks; walking only, the same model puts 128 s3 over 100 C
findings.what_is_written: "At 128 mm the hottest winding peaks at an estimated 62.9-85.9 C, all under the 100 C limit." ... "This over-limit case comes from standing, not walking."
findings.evidence: Script review_d22recheck/reader/scripts/walk_only_temp.py (and stand_share.py) uses the repo's telemetry/thermal.py ThermalNode with each demo_course.json's stored 8 min r_th and C, and each walk_0.25 tau_drive_sq_mean. Walking-only steady temperatures: 128 s3 left_hind_pitch 101.2 C, reaching 100 C after 42.9 min (demo peak 85.9 C; standing supplies only 9 % of its loop heat); 128 s2 left_fore_pitch 99.6 C (demo 81.1 C); 160 s0 left_fore_pitch 110.2 C, reaching 100 C after 22.7 min; 160 s1 right_fore_pitch 101.8 C. This fits the walking ratios of 1.006 and 0.998: the rating, thermal_eq 7.5 N m in sim/data/drives.json, is calibrated to about 100 C steady. The report presents walking as the safe part and the standing posture as the problem. For 160 s0's right hind pitch that is right: walking-only it settles at 64.6 C, and standing supplies 58 % of its heat. But it hides that the standing breaks are what keep the hottest 128 mm windings under 100 C.
